launches.title: Enact: post-training infrastructure for robotics models
launches.tagline: Enact generates the data and evaluations needed to make robotics models reliable in the real world.
launches.body:
**TL;DR: Enact helps teams deploy robots that work in the real world. We roll out policies, generate failure / recovery data, and run in-house evaluations so robots can complete real tasks in production.** 

[**https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dam0tQBIezY**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dam0tQBIezY)

**The Problem**

Robotics models can look flawless in choreographed demos and still fail when an object slips, the scene shifts, or the robot makes an early mistake. Those failures push the policy into states its training data never taught it to recover from. **Robotics models must train on edge cases to be reliable in the real world.**

**What We Built**

Enact turns a policy’s failures into targeted recovery datasets for teams training robotics models. We use the data to fine-tune models and run real-world evaluations, verifying our data improves reliability.

**We’re already serving our first customers: finding where their robots fail and collecting the targeted recovery data needed to make them robust.**

* Roll out an existing model on a physical robot.
* Identify recurring failure states.
* Recreate those states and demonstrate how to recover.
* Retrain with the new trajectories added in.
* Repeat

**Targeted recovery data pushes success rates above 99%.**

On our controlled packing task using pi0.5 on the YAM 6DoF arms:

* 200 ordinary expert demonstrations: 90/100 successful physical rollouts
* 250 ordinary expert demonstrations (more of the same data): 89/100
* 200 expert demonstrations plus 50 targeted recovery demonstrations: 99/100

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109880&key=user_uploads/2406199/e1b83c19-6e1d-4dda-adcf-258398bc1676)

**We’re continuing to longer-horizon tasks such as industrial kitting, lab automation, and electronics recycling**

Longer-horizon tasks need substantially more base and recovery data, but the loop is the same: find failures, target missing behaviors, retrain, repeat.

**Who We Are**

We’re James Stevens and Govind Chada, and we met at Stanford. Govind researched real-world robot adaptation in Chelsea Finn’s IRIS Lab and co-developed recovery methods published at top robotics conferences. Together, we built Enact’s in-house data and evaluation operation and are already serving robotics teams. We started Enact to make robotics models work reliably outside the lab.

**Our Ask**

Training a robot foundation model or deploying a policy that fails on a real task? Tell us the model, task, and where it breaks, and we’ll make it work.

Email: [founders@enact.company](mailto:founders@enact.company)

launches.title: Agency Tool Company: The build and deployment platform for robotics
launches.tagline: Field Robots Faster with ATC Deploy
launches.body:
Today we're sharing Agency Tool Company and our first product, ATC Deploy: a faster, more reliable way to ship software to robots wherever they are. It moves updates up to 20 times faster than docker pull or scp and works with any software stack already in use.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jx0rLRVa06s>

## The updates that took until 2 a.m.

Davis and I spent eight years building Scythe Robotics and putting hundreds of autonomous mowers to work across the country. For years, we deployed software with a tool I'd cobbled together for our first few robots. As the fleet grew, deployment became an ordeal: engineers stayed up until 2 a.m., we coordinated with customers to move robots out of sheds and into LTE coverage at set times, and failed transfers restarted from zero. Shipping a fix could take more coordination than building it. We had models to train and customers to serve, so the tooling limped along with incremental bandaids.

We've since heard the same story from robotics teams across industries. That deployment becomes a hidden bottleneck: teams become release-averse, feedback loops slow and improvements stall. Stitched-together web and IoT tools barely work if you know which scripts to run and who to call, so they survive, even if it means every update is distracting from improving the product.

## What we built

ATC Deploy ships whatever you already run: OS images, Docker images, or any file tree. Run “atc ota push user@robot”, and it sends only the changed bytes, then restarts your software through hooks you define—way faster than a docker push.

Install takes one “curl | sh” command and a config file so you can get back to work fast. Interrupted transfers resume where they stopped, and an offline robot can receive updates by USB if you need. There's no new runtime, packaging format, or operating system to adopt.

## Shipping to robots today

ATC Deploy already ships software to robots at Burro, which has deployed more than 750 machines worldwide, Tempo, polishing concrete across several US states and Canada, and Gather, who is scaling their 99.9% accurate inventory drones nationwide. Their teams spend less time managing delivery and more time improving the robot.

**Operate a robot fleet? Join the ATC Deploy waitlist at [agencytool.com](https://agencytool.com/).** Know a team that should be using it? Send them this post, or to [mailbox@agencytool.com](mailto:mailbox@agencytool.com).

It's time to build robots.

launches.title: 6thSense — Giving Robots Touch
launches.tagline: Giving Robots Touch
launches.body:
6thSense builds wearable tactile sensing rigs that capture how human hands interact with the world — pressure, contact, grip, and pose — across touch, vision, depth, force, and 3D hand pose, all in real environments. We sell that multimodal data to the companies training the next generation of dexterous robots.\
\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gXx53tcIv5U>

Robots are getting good at seeing. They're still terrible at touching. That's because there's almost no data capturing what a hand actually feels while doing real tasks in real homes. Lab data doesn't cut it. We go anywhere and capture the missing layer that manipulation models need to learn fine motor control.

What makes our data different is the hardware we built to collect it. Our tactile sensing devices are designed and manufactured in-house, purpose-built to capture the richest touch signal in the industry — with scale in mind from the very beginning, enabling us to actually solve the tactile data problem. Every sensor maps directly to how robotic skin needs to work: a 1-to-1 analog for the tactile arrays going into the next generation of robot hands. That means the data we collect today doesn't just train better policies. It transfers directly to the hardware it's meant to run on. The team comes from Tesla, Mecka, Samsung, DoorDash, and Amazon, with expertise across hardware, sensors, ML, robotics, and software at scale. If you're training a manipulation policy or need custom tactile data, reach out.

We manufacture Nori: A sub-$2000 bimanual mobile manipulator that can clean rooms, restock shelves, and fold clothes. Nori can handle basic tasks out of the box, and its software lets anyone teach Nori to automate work specific to their home or business. 

Nori aims to solve the robotics data bottleneck. By deploying affordable robots to customers around the world, we can gather the diverse data required to train the next generation of generalist robotic policies. Every user of Nori makes Nori smarter.

Since launching 6 weeks ago we have already deployed our first robot and have over $440k+ in sales.

We can bring general-purpose robotics to homes and businesses that could never afford it before. There are 132.7 million households and 8.4 million employer business locations in the U.S. At $1,688 per robot, selling just one Nori to 0.5% of them represents a $1.2B market opportunity in the U.S. alone.
one_liner: The most capable American-made humanoid robot for $1,688

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
Robots are finally capable enough to be useful, but they're priced like cars, not appliances. A capable humanoid costs $20,000+, so general-purpose robots stay in labs and pilots instead of homes. 

It's a big problem because household labor is one of the largest unpriced markets in the world. Today's answer is a stack of single-task machines, a dishwasher, a washer, a vacuum, each $600 to $1,000 and doing exactly one thing. Whoever ships a general-purpose robot at appliance prices doesn't win a niche, they open consumer robotics the way the PC opened computing.

We're robotics researchers from Columbia (RoboPIL, CGUI). After years watching \[$100K research robots struggle with tasks cheap hardware could handle\], we realized the gap between lab robots and home robots isn't intelligence, it's cost discipline. Nobody was going to fix that from inside a lab, so we left to build it: a $1,688 robot anyone can teach.

launches.title: Neuromorphic - Building an embodiment-agnostic “brain” that makes robots fast to deploy
launches.tagline: We make robots smarter, and faster to deploy. Starting with wet labs!
launches.body:
Hi everyone! We’re Cem, Ege, and Vatan, the founders of Neuromorphic 👋\
\
**TL;DR** Neuromorphic is building an embodiment-agnostic “brain” that makes robots fast to deploy, and easy to manage through natural interfaces like Slack, email, and phone. Our goal is to make deploying robots in wet labs and other physical industries as easy as onboarding a new employee.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6T0BDyjakmo>\
\
**The Problem**\
To make robotics mainstream, we believe two problems have to be resolved:\
1\. Deployment: Robots are still too slow, expensive, and engineering-intensive to deploy and adapt to new tasks and environments.\
2\. Interaction: Managing and controlling robots remains too technical.\
\
**What We’ve Built**\
Neuromorphic packages sensors, compute, and software into a “brain” that can be attached to any robot body. An onboard LLM orchestrator turns natural-language instructions into workflows made up of reusable robotic skills, such as navigating, picking up an object, opening a refrigerator, or inspecting an area. Individual skills can be of various types; they could be AI models we develop, like Vision-Language Models and Video Action Models, or just plain code. Sensor-based safety loops monitor every action to ensure reliable execution.

We are also giving robots emails, phone numbers, and Slack access to make human-robot interaction more intuitive than using dashboards. The robots then respond to queries and take actions using the onboard LLM.\
\
**Traction**\
Within a week of our first conversation with a leading biotechnology company, we deployed our robot in their wet lab, which is capable of operating autonomously 24/7, and already completed over 1500 tasks.\
\
**The Team**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109550&key=user_uploads/3607343/b28b023b-f328-4c5d-9181-720e96e5b1a3)

\
Cem: Second-time founder and did robotics research at Cambridge University. Previously built LLM routing and training acceleration, and did precision robotics.\
\
Vatan: Maintained multiple open-source robotics libraries, most notably MoveIt, one of the most popular motion-planning frameworks for robotics. Led various teams in robotics startups from Series A to Series C in Japan and Singapore. Deployed over a thousand robots.\
\
Ege: Did Robotics and AI research at Bilkent University. Research fellow at Nanyang Technological University. Published research in top AI and robotics conferences. Won HackMIT in 2024.\
\
Cem and Ege first met as teammates in the FIRST Robotics Competition. They reached out to Vatan for mentorship and robotics advice. We spent the next three years building robots and winning competitions together. We remained close and eventually reunited to start Neuromorphic!\
\
**Ask**\
We're looking for warm intros to wet lab, biotech, and physical-industry operators. If you have a repetitive physical process and have wondered whether a robot could do it, email us at [founders@neuromorphic.vision](mailto:founders@neuromorphic.vision) or [book a call here](https://cal.com/team/neuromorphic/meet-the-founders-of-neuromorphic).

name: Ultrasonium
long_description:
The technologies that define this century, including data centers, rockets, satellites, and robots, are built from complex metal parts. As these systems advance, the parts get harder to make. Past a certain complexity, casting and machining stop working, and the advanced methods that remain are slow, expensive, and hazardous.

Ultrasonium has invented a new manufacturing method to make these critical parts 15x faster and 75% cheaper than the methods they replace, in the U.S. and at scale. Solid metal feedstock goes in and a finished part safely comes out, controlled by a physical AI layer and novel control processes. 

The systems that matter most, in aerospace, energy, and compute, are demanding metal geometries that can't be machined or cast and are too expensive and slow to make with incumbent methods, at a moment when domestic manufacturing capacity is a national priority.

Our founding team has built and innovated some of the most complex engineering systems known to man: quantum computers, superconductors, nuclear reactors, and novel aerospace alloy processing methods.
one_liner: Metal manufacturing, faster, cheaper, and more versatile.

launches.tagline: Deploy robots that learn new tasks from a single human demonstration in the factory
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** We deploy robots that learn new tasks from a single human demonstration in the factory. A new task shows up on the floor? You just film it once on your phone and the robot picks it up. No sitting around collecting data. No engineer flying out to your site. No overnight fine-tuning. You show it, and the robot learns.

<https://youtu.be/OoQvOGrycDg>

**❌ The problem**

Manufacturing is full of constantly changing, high-mix production tasks, which are among the hardest to automate. A line that's packing one product today is building something completely different next week. Every factory owner we talk to says the same two things: they can't find enough people to do the work, and the automation solutions they've tried have been too expensive and too rigid, often ending up gathering dust in a corner.

**✅ What we do**

We're developing a robot foundation model whose core capability is adapting instantly to new variations of a task. You give the model a human demonstration video as context, and it bridges the embodiment gap to execute the task itself. This in-context learning is the missing piece in today's VLA approaches, and it's what changing manufacturing environments need.

We deliver the complete system: robot hardware, foundation model, and on-site deployment. We're already deploying robots at customer sites.

**👋 Who we are**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110367&key=user_uploads/585458/0832cd2d-2dfc-41b0-8de6-d29897b6c8d3)

Between the two of us, we have 20+ years of experience in robotics. Navid was part of the core team that productized Spot at Boston Dynamics and led manipulation projects there; before that, he was at Rethink Robotics. Mojtaba led whole-body control and bimanual manipulation efforts at Amazon Robotics and was a Research Assistant Professor at Northwestern University.

**🙏 Our ask**

Do you have a manufacturing task that needs automating, or know someone who does? Let us know and we'll automate it.

name: Grip
long_description: Grip is a robotics company building intelligent robotic systems for waste and recycling. We are starting with organic waste, where removing contaminants from messy, constantly changing streams remains difficult and highly manual. Our technology combines learning-based manipulation and custom hardware to identify and pick objects, learning from real-world operating data, including every successful and failed grasp, to become more reliable and adaptable over time. This helps waste operators reduce manual sorting, recover more valuable material, lower contamination, and deploy automation flexibly across facilities. Over time, Grip aims to expand beyond organics and build the intelligent manipulation layer for trash in general, making waste processing and the circular economy more efficient and scalable.

launches.title: Grip - Robotics for Waste Management
launches.tagline: Robots that sort any waste and recover recyclables, learning from every grasp.
launches.body:
Hi everyone - Stan and Jonas here, founders of **Grip**. We build intelligent robots that sort _any_ waste, not just the clean, predictable objects existing systems are limited to. We're starting with plastic contamination in organic waste.\
\
<https://youtu.be/qIJ4a49WxpI>

**The problem**

We didn't start with a thesis, we found it on sorting lines, after visiting waste facilities across several countries:

* **Contamination is existential.** Plastic that organic-waste facilities can't remove gets shredded, processed, and spread onto agricultural soil. Operators spend up to 30% of operating costs fighting it and still fall short. Even Germany's 0.1% limit for plastic in finished compost is a tacit admission that full removal isn't possible with today's tools.
* **The labor force is aging and shrinking.** The picking work is unpleasant and turnover is brutal. Operators increasingly aren't choosing between people and robots. They're choosing between robots and nobody.
* **Dangerous items cause fires.** Batteries, propane tanks, and vapes slip through and ignite during handling and shredding: 448 reported fires at US and Canadian waste facilities in 2025, \~$2.5B in damage, and insurers are walking away. At the same time trash sorting is sitting in the top 5 of US deadliest occupations.

**What we built**

The hard part isn't the gripper. It's that waste never looks the way you planned. Objects arrive crushed, folded, tangled, half-buried, and moving. Put today's sorting robots in front of this and they break.

We're building one manipulation system that picks whatever shows up, at the front of the line where the material is most chaotic and existing automation stops. That means chaotic scene understanding, robust grasp planning, and hardware built for real waste streams: our custom three-way gripper is designed to maximize throughput, taking out as much contamination per cycle as possible.

Our rugged hardware matters, but intelligence is the product. Every pick generates data no other system ever encounters: what the robot saw, what it tried, how the material responded, whether it worked.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111317&key=user_uploads/3678142/bc867fdc-9225-4b85-83f9-f83433465d5b)

**Why now**

Waste policy has moved from vague ambition to enforceable deadlines:

* Separate bio-waste collection is now mandatory across the EU. More material, and more contamination, every year.
* New EU fertiliser rules just cut permitted impurities in compost and digestate, with national limits like Germany's stricter still.
* The US is real: California mandated a 75% cut in landfilled organics, missed it, and enforcement is ramping. At the same time, landfills near major cities are filling up, and that pressure is pushing more and more US municipalities to collect organic waste separately. More material, more contamination, more facilities that need to sort it.

More than 6,500 biowaste plants and thousands of recycling facilities across Europe and North America face this with no robot that can touch it. That's Grip.

**Why us**

We've built autonomous race cars, quadrupeds, drones, and excavators, robots that operate in dirt, weather, and chaos rather than controlled labs. Grip is that experience applied to an industry where physical intelligence removes a real bottleneck.

**Our ask**

We'd love intros to:

* Owners and operators of composting, anaerobic-digestion, and organic-waste facilities
* Owners and operators of MRFs and recycling facilities
* Regulators and experts shaping contamination limits and recycling standards

If someone runs a facility and will show us their hardest sorting problem, we'll get on a plane.

launches.body:
# \*\*\*\*

**TLDR;**

* **Hebbian Robotics builds APIs for searching and analyzing Physical AI data at scale**
* Our APIs enable data providers to get **on-demand signals and metrics** on the quality of their data, without managing infrastructure
* We help our customers evaluate data quality without training a robotics model

<https://youtu.be/ffvFNs3bjbs>

**Our Ask**

* Buyers want data they can trust. If you're selling egocentric or robot data, **Let’s Chat ([https://calendly.com/brandon-hebbianrobotics/30min](https://calendly.com/brandon-hebbianrobotics/30min)**) and we'll show you how quality signals and metrics help you sell more at higher prices
* **Check out Pareto ([https://pareto.hebbianrobotics.com/](https://pareto.hebbianrobotics.com/)),** an example of how our APIs can be used

### **Who We Are**

* We’re Brandon and Kingston, we've trained AI models for industrial cleaning robots and built production systems for camera fleets across the globe
* [**Brandon Ong**](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/388120)'s previous AI startup was backed by Sequoia. He did research on AI for low resource languages that topped Stanford’s LLM benchmark, SEA-HELM, and dropped out of his joint PhD in Robotics at Columbia and NTU
* [**Kingston Kuan**](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/968709) spent years at Jane Street building systems that scaled to millions of messages per second. At Verkada, he worked on their core video surveillance platform that processed large scale multimodal data

### **The Problem**

* **High quality data is the bottleneck for unlocking the next frontier of intelligence in robotics**
* Buyers want **data they can trust** 
* Data providers don’t have the bandwidth to provide signals and metrics about the quality of their data when they are **focused on** **operational excellence**  
* This means that **model developers are forgoing model improvements due to a lack of high quality data**, impeding progress in robotics

### **Our Solution**

* APIs for searching and analyzing Physical AI data at scale that enables providers to get **on-demand signals and metrics on data quality**
* Buyers demanding per-collector hour limits? **Prove compliance while we stay ahead of the workarounds**
* Changed standard operating procedures for collection? **Monitor for quality drift and regression**
* Suspect duplicate samples? **Verify quickly with a single API call**

launches.body:
Hey BF 👋 We are [@Joohyun (CJ) Cha](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/1720857) and [@Robin Lee](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2574843), cofounders of [@Dawn Industries](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/33344). We’re building **VIM**, Automatic Diagnosis & Fix for Industrial Automation Cells.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109744&key=user_uploads/2574843/10398df4-83d1-4d24-860a-5ede83b91f9c)

# **TL;DR:**

**VIM is Sentry for industrial automation cells. When a cell faults, VIM reads the error code and the live machine signals, digs the root cause out of the OEM manuals and the cell's own history, and stages one safe fix for the operator to approve. When a CNC drifts, VIM catches it with the machine's own probe seconds after the cut and stages the offset correction. Downtime goes from hours to about a minute; scrap gets caught at part one instead of final inspection.**

Watch how **VIM** works:

Robot Cell Video: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JfGQjorNS2U>

CNC Machine Video: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fgNPOtBLku8>

# WHAT WE BUILT

VIM sits on the cell and closes the loop from fault to recovery:

1. **Connect**. Reads **PLC**, **HMI**, **robot**, **CNC**, **sensor**, and **driver state** without touching the controls you already trust.
2. **Understand**. Matches the fault to live signals, the right page of the right manual, and this cell's own prior recoveries or trends the probe touches and traces drift to tool wear, thermal growth, a bumped fixture.
3. **Recover**. Stages one bounded, validated action: a restart, a parameter change, an offset correction. The operator approves it like a pull request.

Before anything moves, the safety chain is verified: interlocks, light curtain, area scanner. VIM cannot bypass it; that's a precondition in the action policy, not a feature. And when the fault is genuinely hardware, VIM routes the incident to the right person with the exact diagnosis and repair steps attached, instead of a generic alarm and a prayer.

**Autonomy is earned, not assumed**: VIM ships read-only, then one-click approval, then unattended recovery only on fault classes where it has earned trust. And it's mixed-vendor by design (FANUC robots and CNC controls, Universal Robots, Siemens, Allen-Bradley, Cognex, Keyence, Renishaw probes), because a cell is multi-vendor by definition and a copilot that speaks one vendor's language can't close the loop.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109744&key=user_uploads/2574843/83b531fe-5737-4f94-8b70-cd37330dae7c)

# TEAM

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109744&key=user_uploads/2574843/df76af6e-3516-4d76-9081-145424822ef3)

We're four people covering both halves of the problem.

[Robin Lee](https://www.linkedin.com/in/robinlee02/) and [Joohyun (CJ) Cha](https://www.linkedin.com/in/joohyun-cha), cofounders, Robin was the founding AI engineer at an aviation AI startup, and built the production AI systems behind its $10M Series A and a 1st-place Minister's Award from Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT. CJ cofounded Zipper as CTO (acquired by MetaZone), did ML on genomic data at Avalo. We spent the past years in plants and machine shops learning all the faults and error that happen during manufacturing processes.

Our founding engineers, come from Tesla and robotics research labs. They spent years building and fixing automation cells and various robot cases.

# OUR ASK

* **Intros to plant managers, manufacturing engineers, and controls engineers** at plants running robot cells (palletizing, case packing, welding, machine tending, inspection). If a stopped line ruins their week, we want to meet them.
* **Intros to machining and quality leaders at plants and shops (primarily aerospace & defense) running CNCs**, anywhere scrap gets discovered at final inspection instead of at the machine.
* **War stories.** Tell us about the cell that keeps stopping or the machine that keeps drifting. Best case, we make it your most reliable one.

Reach us at [joohyun_cha@dawnxr.com](mailto:joohyun_cha@dawnxr.com) or 401-226-3503, or book a demo at <https://dawnxr.com>.

name: Robocurve
long_description:
Robocurve builds open-source tools and independent benchmarks to measure how well robots can do real-world jobs. Instead of relying on unverified demo videos from frontier labs, we score their models on reproducible benchmarks that anyone can trust.

Today there are no well-run, standardized robotics benchmarks. Labs evaluate in-house, and no independent group has stepped in to run continuous benchmarking as a service. The result is that no one actually knows how good anyone else is, or where the real frontier sits.

Good benchmarks require operating and maintaining physical hardware and real-world setups. Simulation only goes so far, since models that look strong in sim can show large performance gaps once deployed in the real world. Building real-world benchmarks means coordinating job-domain experts, evals engineering, and hands-on robotics all at once.

Frontier labs are targeting general-purpose robotics by 2028, yet the field of robotics evals barely exists. Whoever builds the trusted measure of robot capability becomes the reference everyone relies on. We combine backgrounds in AI evals and robotics to build and grow this field as fast as possible. We already shipped v1 of our open-source framework, Inspect Robots, and ran our first pilot scoring a frontier model on a real robot.
one_liner: Evals for robots

Called the 2024 election correctly in all 50 states. Won a Rhodes Scholarship. Gold medal at the International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics.

launches.title: Robocurve — Real-World Evaluations of Physical AI
launches.tagline: Real-world evals for robots
launches.body:
Hi, I’m [Jay](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jeqcho/), co-founder of [Robocurve](http://robocurve.org). We measure and reports what frontier robots can actually do in the real world.

Our launch video <https://youtu.be/Cjkt2ikvsiQ>

Frontier labs are racing to build general-purpose robots within two years, yet no one knows what today's robots are truly capable of. Demo videos of robots performing narrow, cherry-picked tasks proliferate, but there are no rigorous, continuous, standardized benchmarks for robotics.

Robocurve builds benchmarks for robots and the AI models that control them, to help the world understand how far robotics has come and how fast it's moving. Our benchmarks range from playing Jenga and making a sandwich to constructing a data center.

General-purpose robots could arrive before the end of the decade, with far-reaching implications: accelerated data center buildouts, explosive economic growth from a fully automated economy, and intensified geopolitical competition between the US and China. Real-world evaluations from Robocurve will help clarify the timeline to general-purpose robots so that society can prepare for their arrival well ahead of time.

[Jay](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jeqcho/) is a Rhodes Scholar and a top contributor to UK AI Security Institute's Inspect Evals. He has published papers in ICML, EMNLP, ACL, ACM EC and his research has been featured in MIT Technology Review. Previously, he spent time at AWS Bedrock, MATS, and Harvard where he completed his BA and MA with a highest honors thesis on AI and democracy.

If you build robots or AI models, reach out! We'd love to put them to the test. Learn more at [robocurve.org](http://robocurve.org).

launches.body:
We're [Caleb](https://www.linkedin.com/in/caleb-horan) and [Janak](https://www.linkedin.com/in/janak-panthi), PhD roboticists from UT Austin. We've spent a combined 15 years in nuclear, 10 of which deploying autonomous robots at Los Alamos National Lab, and we're building Salem Robotics.\
**TLDR:** Our software turns robots into independent survey and inspection workers at your facility.

[Launch Video](https://youtu.be/7xObOE6knZM)

## **Life and death pain worth $Millions/year**

At every nuclear facility, highly trained radiation-protection teams spend hours each day walking the site, filling out hand-drawn maps, and searching for something life-threatening: radiation. IN THE BEST CASE they find nothing, and still have to return to their posts to transcribe the data into a computer before doing the actual high-value work they were assigned. These surveys are time-consuming, dangerous, expensive, and prone to data inconsistencies that carry direct regulatory consequences.

The same pain exists well beyond nuclear. Whether it's gas-leak inspection or ammonia surveys, similar workflows run across oil, gas, chemical, biological, space, and other hazardous facilities.

## **What we do**

An operator defines the work from a simple dashboard; the robot then navigates the site, handles instruments, opens doors, turns valves, collects measurements, and generates structured, auditable, compliance-ready reports. We're hardware-agnostic, so plants run our software on robots they already own, many of which sit in a closet today as "$200k paperweights, " or we can provide the right robot for the job. Our stack is designed for safety-critical infrastructure and comes with theoretical safety guarantees, exactly what regulators and plant leadership require. Our core manipulation framework was not possible before and is based on **breakthrough founder research** published and presented at the most prestigious IEEE journals and conferences in the world. 

We're already in active contract-scoping conversations across the nuclear industry and oil & gas.

**Our asks**

* Intros to operations or innovation leaders in nuclear or similar hazardous sites (oil, gas, chem, bio, space).
* Advice from founders who've sold into safety-critical industrial environments.
* Sites where routine surveys are frequent, hard to staff, or particularly painful? We'd love to hear about them.

Comments, Emails, and DMs welcome. \

name: Hemlock
long_description:
Every serious robotics lab is bottlenecked on the same thing: demonstration data. The field has converged on egocentric video and hand pose as the substrate, and both are now cheap to collect at scale. What neither of them contains is force. A video of someone picking up an egg and a video of someone picking up a rock are nearly identical in pixel space and nearly identical in joint angles. They differ almost entirely in a quantity nobody is recording. Policies trained without it learn geometry and inherit no sense of touch.

Hemlock closes that gap at the source. Our device, the Bracelet, is a wrist-worn surface EMG band that reads the electrical activity of the forearm muscles that actually drive the hand, which means it recovers contraction force directly rather than inferring it from motion. This distinction is the whole thesis: force cannot be reconstructed downstream of kinematics, because a hand squeezing hard isometrically and a hand resting can occupy the identical pose. Muscle signal is the only non-invasive channel that separates them.
one_liner: Force-sensing wristband for training robotic AI

launches.title: Dreamscale Labs: Running robot brains in the cloud
launches.tagline: The fastest cloud inference platform for robotics.
launches.body:
**TL;DR: We're 40-50% faster than existing cloud providers in serving frontier robot AI models, e.g. DreamZero, MolmoAct2.**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jVqvJFBRcd0>

\[1x speed, autonomous\]

DSL is building the fastest cloud inference platform for robotics. We let you deploy physical AI without needing expensive local GPUs.

Robot foundation models are growing more and more computationally expensive. The latest frontier of robotics no longer fits feasibly on local GPUs. Compute costs keep soaring amidst a global LPDDR shortage; NVIDIA just doubled the prices of Jetsons in July.

**We're taking a contrarian bet that the future is moving inference _off the robot_ and _into the cloud._**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=115448&key=user_uploads/3499827/4ca20fc9-00a8-4043-bc43-d51b8b5d0cbf)

How do we do this? We work across the full stack of robot inference to push latency down:

* Model-level architectural adjustments for faster inference
* Kernel-level optimizations to maximally leverage server-grade GPUs
* Network-level optimizations for fast and reliable transport over the cloud
* Region-specific compute allocation to ensure the shortest physical distance between the servers and our customers' robots

These optimizations enable us to be **8% faster** than NVIDIA's implementation **at half the GPU count** (320ms vs 350ms, for DreamZero 14B).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=115448&key=user_uploads/3499827/69393040-ca17-41cd-a1fb-cd5d70176921)

Furthermore, something we noticed for robotics companies with fast R&D cycles was that their GPUs had long idle periods with concentrated bursts of inference traffic. We're one of the first companies in the world to offer on-demand pricing for physical AI inference, giving users more flexibility with the cost.

We're already working closely with a range of early partners across deployment, research and evaluation. In full FDE spirit, we collaborate with our customers to custom-fit inference stacks that address their unique deployment challenges. We help you get your robot AI to deployment faster.

Our mission is to democratize access to frontier physical intelligence, and we believe cloud is the way forward. You can read our thesis here:

•⁠ ⁠<http://dreamscalelabs.com/blog/why>

\
